SENIOR CO-OPS: NOT YET.

Austin Housing staff recommends holding off on pursuing senior cooperative housing for now.

In an October 23 memo, the department closes out a Council request to explore shared-equity housing for seniors and people with disabilities on City-owned land, particularly near transit.

Staff says cooperative housing remains a viable model to evaluate for individual sites. But current considerations include market demand, development costs, site accessibility and the organizational capacity needed to operate a resident-governed community.

Feedback from City-supported senior properties also points to challenges involving unit size, location and referral pathways. Unexpected repairs and vacancies can put financial pressure on remaining cooperative members.

For Austin residents and families planning ahead, this is an update on the City's housing strategy. The memo does not announce a new senior co-op development or application opportunity. Staff says these models will continue to be considered during future site assessments.

Source: Austin Housing, staff memo dated October 23, 2026.
